[Thu Sep 10 #eng] alex: For that group DM edge case, what does the user see if the agent is added late? Does it get history or start blank? Asking for the onboarding copy.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: Right now it starts blank. History backfill is the part I'm tracing, since it touches the same permission check as the other DM cases.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: Policy for the permission check, so we're all building against the same rule: agents never read a DM unless a participant forwards it. That covers late-added agents too, so blank start is correct, no backfill.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] alex: Got it, I'll write the late-add copy around a blank start. Should the agent post a short note saying it can't see earlier messages?
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: A note works, but keep it generic. It shouldn't hint at what was said earlier, only that the agent joined late.

[Thu Sep 10 #eng] oli: Memory store still unchecked. aj, do you have a baseline yet for concurrent reads on shared memory with lots of agents active?
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] alex: Love the fake chatter idea. Should the sandbox agents have names and personalities so people can tell them apart at a glance? Maybe a little name card at the demo table?
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: No baseline yet. I have a read-heavy test script but it only simulates a handful of agents. Need to scale it up first.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] oli: There's an agent-sim harness in the runtime tests that spawns fake agents with canned channel traffic. Might save you rebuilding. Check if it fits your script.

[Thu Sep 10 #eng] aj: Thanks, I'll try the sim harness for the load test. Also, on DM permissions: I'll merge the forwarded-DM permission check by Tue Sep 15, late-add edge case included.
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] alex: Ooh, unprompted jump-in is the best demo. Should we seed a thread where two humans are stuck on something, so the agent has a natural reason to chime in?
[Thu Sep 10 #eng] frida: Related to the load test: one partner runs a ton of agents in a single workspace and said memory lookups felt laggy during their Monday standup rush.

[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] theo: Do I rerun every baseline from scratch, or just rescore the surviving tasks from the saved traces? Rescoring would be way faster for the slow scaffolds.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: Rescoring is fine for tasks whose test harness didn't change. Any task we patch to drop near-duplicate overlap needs a fresh run, though.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] marcus: Near-duplicate check is doable. I'll run fuzzy matching on the solution diffs against the fork and gist dumps, then flag anything above a similarity cutoff.
[Mon Oct 12 #harbor] yuki: Updating the eval config now to point at v1.3. Patched tasks get fresh runs, the rest can reuse saved traces. I'll flag which is which in the config.
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Once the swap list is final I'll rerun the baselines and plot pass rate by repo size. Curious if multi-file tasks widen the gap between models.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: Theo, if you plot by repo size, bucket by files touched too. Otherwise size and multi-file get tangled and the gap is hard to read.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Good call, will do. I'll also split by language since the Python tasks tend to be the easiest, so that might be another confound.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Found a couple of multi-file candidates in a Rust build tool, bug spans the parser and the config loader. Checking the license now.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: Rust is useful there too. If the models do much worse on those, I'd want to report language as its own breakdown in the paper.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Rust tasks would be a good breakdown. Since the paper's due Oct 30, I'll plan to have the baseline reruns done a few days before so we have time to write up the language split.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Rust build tool license came back permissive, so those candidates are usable. The fix touches the parser and config loader together, and the tests are deterministic.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] elena: Rust builds will be slow in the sandbox. I'll check the image has the toolchain cached so timeouts don't masquerade as model failures.
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Baselines table is still on the old task set. I'll regenerate once the replacements land, otherwise the numbers won't line up with the new items.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Two of the overlapping tasks are near-verbatim from a popular CLI repo. Leaning toward dropping those outright rather than rewriting them, since the solutions are easy to find.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] felix: Release note for planning: the harbor release version is v1.2. It'll carry the contamination replacements once marcus's list is final, so the changelog stays in one place.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If marcus drops those two CLI tasks, I'll check the difficulty spread afterward. Don't want the replacements skewing easy and inflating pass rates.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Good point on difficulty. The replacement candidates I've pulled so far are mostly single-file fixes, so they'd probably skew easy. I'll look for some multi-file ones.
---
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Two of the Rust candidates look like they share a fixture directory, so I'll check they don't leak each other's expected outputs before they go in.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] yuki: If they do share a fixture directory, I'd rather split it per task than drop either one. Cleaner isolation and we keep the multi-file case.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] marcus: Splitting per task works. I'll copy the shared fixtures into each task's own directory and diff the expected outputs afterward to confirm nothing carried over.
[Mon Oct 5 #harbor] theo: Once the split fixtures are in, I'll rerun the baseline on those Rust tasks so we can see if isolation shifts any scores.
---

[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: Split the import-error bucket out of the multi-file plots. Spread tightens a lot without it. Will rerun properly once more cached images land.

[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] yuki: Fine by me. Should we report environment failures as a separate rate per slice, so readers see how much each slice is affected?
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: Yes, per-slice rate works. I'll add it to the results table. Also, I put in the draft that the release gate is 75% pass@1, so the environment-failure rate sits right next to it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] theo: nice, that matches what I saw on my branch. once the patch works, add a test with a hyphenated pool name so it doesn't regress.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] elena: One of the native-extension repos needs a system lib missing from the base image. Patching that now, so the cached image for it is slower than the others.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] felix: Cached image digests should go in the manifest too, so anyone rerunning gets the exact same environment. I'll add a field for it.
[Wed Oct 7 #harbor-evals] elena: patch works, stuck jobs scheduled right away. adding the hyphenated pool test now, then I'll requeue the dropped batch.
